items.title: ⚡️ Match nested included routers in a single pass
items.author: danielshtel
items.body:
Fixes the slowdown with nested routers reported in #16620.

Since 0.137, routing a request walks the router tree several times: `_get_routes_version()` walks the whole subtree on every call, and each level matches its subtree again in `handle()`.

* A router change now also bumps the version of the routers that include it, so checking the version doesn't walk the tree.
* Each included router caches the flat list of routes in its subtree and matches it once per request. `matches()` passes the matched route to `handle()` in the child scope.
* Routers that override `matches()` or `handle()`, and routes that override `matches()`, are still called as before.

items.author: mgkvibez

## Description

The WebSockets page doesn't mention that WebSocket handlers are always `async def`: unlike *path operation functions*, there's no plain `def` option where FastAPI runs the function in an external threadpool. Because of this, users coming from HTTP endpoints naturally assume the same `def`-threadpool escape hatch exists, run blocking code in a WebSocket handler, and freeze every other connection in the app.

items.title: Fix OpenAPI generation with more than 128 parameter models
items.author: stupidprogrammer4
items.body:
Generating `/openapi.json` with 129 distinct parameter models raises `KeyError: ModelField(...)`. The same app works with 128 models. This affects query, header and cookie models, and reproduces on current master.

`get_cached_model_fields()` uses the default 128-entry LRU cache, while `ModelField` is identity-hashed. Schema collection and parameter rendering traverse the models separately. Once models are evicted, the second traversal creates different fields and cannot find their entries in `field_mapping`.

Use `functools.cache` so a model keeps the same field objects across both traversals. This retains fields for the lifetime of each cached model; applications that dynamically create unbounded model classes would retain those entries as well.

items.author: piotrszyma

Reported in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16221.

items.title: ✅ Share one portal across websocket sessions in tutorial003 test
items.author: grahamc
items.body:
`test_websocket_handle_disconnection` can hang on a loaded machine.

With a bare `TestClient(app)`, each `websocket_connect()` gets its own portal and event loop.
The chat example broadcasts from one session's handler onto the other session's socket, which wakes the other loop from the wrong thread.
If that loop is already blocked in `epoll_wait`, it never wakes and the test deadlocks.
Details and reproducer: https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/discussions/3697

Entering the `TestClient` gives every session one shared portal, so cross-session sends are same-loop operations.
The `time.sleep()` workarounds are no longer needed.

items.title: 🐛 Ensure SSE endpoint generators and checkpoint streams are closed on client disconnect
items.author: VimalN2005
items.body:
### Discussion

- Proposed and confirmed in Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16346

---

### Description

In `fastapi/routing.py`, when handling Server-Sent Events (`EventSourceResponse`), the `_producer` task consumes `sse_aiter` and forwards events to `send_stream`.

When a client disconnects while the producer is awaiting `send_stream.send(...)`, the task group cancels the producer task. Because `sse_aiter` was never explicitly closed upon cancellation, the generator's `finally` cleanup block (e.g. database session teardown, locks, or external resources) would not run deterministically until garbage collection or loop termination.

items.title: fix: serialize WebSocket validation errors to JSON string in close reason
items.author: RushikeshTelrandhe
items.body:
The default `websocket_request_validation_exception_handler` currently passes the result of `jsonable_encoder(exc.errors())` directly to `WebSocket.close()` as the `reason`.

`jsonable_encoder(exc.errors())` returns a list, while `WebSocket.close()` expects `reason` to be a `str | None`. As a result, WebSocket request-validation errors can cause the exception handler itself to fail instead of closing the connection with the intended `1008` policy-violation code.

This change serializes the validation errors with `json.dumps()` before passing them to `WebSocket.close()`. The reason is therefore a valid string containing machine-readable JSON.

A regression test was added to verify that:

- WebSocket request-validation failures close with code `1008`.
- The close reason is a string.

items.author: Noxtimo
items.body:
Fixes #15312

When a client disconnects while FastAPI is reading the request body, Starlette raises `starlette.requests.ClientDisconnect`. items.author: TrueFurina

Fixes #14574

**Problem**: when using Form models, `_get_multidict_value()` returns the field default for fields not present in the form data. That default is then passed to Pydantic, so every field appears in `model_fields_set` even when it was not provided, and validation is enforced on unprovided defaults.

items.title: fix: strip path converter suffix in get_path_param_names
items.author: TrueFurina
items.body:
Fixes #14883

**Problem**: `get_path_param_names()` uses `re.findall("{(.*?)}", path)`, so a route like `/{param:path}` extracts `param:path` (including the converter suffix). When the parameter is declared implicitly (without `Path()`), it is not recognized as a path parameter and the request fails.

**Fix**: strip everything after `:` in each extracted name, so `{param:path}` is recognized as `param`. Plain `{param}` is unaffected.

items.title: Inherit Starlette router dispatch
items.author: Kludex
items.body:
## Summary

Remove FastAPI's copy of `Router.app()` and express low-priority frontend routing through Starlette's existing `default` callback.

Starlette remains responsible for lifespan handling, normal route matching, partial matches, and slash redirects. FastAPI handles low-priority routes only after Starlette finds no regular route or redirect, then delegates to the original default application.

items.title: fix: make _fallback_file_exists async to avoid blocking event loop with sync I/O
items.author: VimalN2005
items.body:
Fixes the event loop blocking issue discussed in #16213.

### Description
The `_fallback_file_exists` helper in `_FrontendStaticFiles` is called during the request path when `fallback="auto"` is configured. However, it was calling the synchronous `lookup_path` method directly on the asyncio event loop thread. 

This PR converts `_fallback_file_exists` into an `async def` coroutine and offloads the synchronous file system checks to a worker thread using `run_in_threadpool`, ensuring the event loop is never blocked by fallback existence checks.
